properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean formation composed of Lower Carboniferous sedimentary rock of the Gullane and Wardie Mudstone Formations, interspersed with nearby volcanic basaltic intrusions. Structural load rests upon stiff glaciomarine till over sandstone bedrock. Primary building fabric comprises fine-grained Carboniferous quartz-arenite sourced from local historic quarries: buff-coloured Craigleith sandstone alongside laminated pink-grey Hailes sandstone. Bedding and pointing utilize traditional hot-mixed lime mortar composed of slaked high-calcium quicklime and sharp fluvial aggregate.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Peripheral urban specimens of *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Canopy state for late September displays early autumn phenology: dense crowns transitioning from deep green to muted ochre and olive-yellow margins, with localized foliage thinning along upper outer branches.

properties.architectural_summary: Victorian Scots Baronial and Italian Renaissance Revival mixed-use tenement blocks alongside early Victorian Georgian infill. Facades range from 4 to 5 storeys plus mansard and dormered attic storeys. Massing features strapwork and crow-stepped gables, corbelled corner turrets, canted oriel bay stacks, and molded continuous stringcourses. Fenestration consists of timber-framed 1-over-1 and 2-over-2 sliding sash-and-case windows set in planar ashlar reveals. In the mid-distance rises the Italian Romanesque campanile of St George's West Church (David Bryce, 1869), defined by a tall square-plan sandstone tower, round-arched louvred belfry arcades, a bracketed cornice, and an octagonal spire.
